newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Call buying picks up in U.S. T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call buying picks up in U.S. T-bonds.

text.p: A flurry of call buying in U.S. Treasury bond options preceeded a runup in the underlying futures this morning, options traders said.
"There was a lot of directional buying in calls. Those who bought these things had a good idea that the market was going up," said a Treasury floor broker for a U.S. brokerage firm.

The buying was concentrated in July options in the 110-00 and 111-00 strikes, brokers said. One large U.S. brokerage house bought 3,500 July 111-00 calls, while another house bought 1,500 of the calls. Two Wall Street dealer firms bought about 1,000 July 110-00 calls apiece.
September Treasury bond futures ended the session about 3/4 point higher, after firmly rejecting the day's low of 108-29 and then setting off a series of buy-stops, floor traders said.
In futures, dealers as well as local traders who had been big sellers early in the session turned around and bought back those contracts as the rally gained momentum, traders said.
Yet implied volatilities for bond options were little changed, underscoring the directional bent to the day's activity, they said.
Trading volume in bond options had slumped over the past several days as the lack of volatility caused interest to dry up.
"That's reflecting the fact that volatility has not been going anywhere," said the floor broker. He pegged the week's range in July volatility at 8.2 to 8.5 percent.
July ended the session unchanged from the previous close at 8.30 percent, down 0.1 point from the morning. September was 8.4 percent, below Thursday's 8.50 percent.
